reflog, not ORIG_HEAD (which unstaging or a stash overwrites): walking back from
the newest entry, resets that did not move HEAD are skipped, and the tip the
last real reset left is where the dropped work starts. Dropped means only that
tip reaches it: commits HEAD, a remote or another branch still reach (merged-in
main, a teammate's commit an undone rebase brought in) are never inherited,
while a backup branch pointing at the tip itself does not count. A dropped
commit's trailers are carried into the new message when every staged file it
changed has exactly the content it had at that tip (read from the index git is
preparing the commit in, so `git commit -a` and path-limited commits compare
what they commit), so an agent's ten commits
redone as three logical ones keep every checkpoint, each on the commit that now
holds its files, while one coincidentally identical file (a lockfile, an empty
`__init__.py`, the same deletion) among rewritten ones inherits nothing. Commits
made since the reset keep the redo open only while each of them redid some of
the dropped work; any other ref operation (checkout, merge, rebase, pull) ends
it. Folding with `git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git commit --amend` inherits the
folded commit's trailers too. Inherited trailers are links, exactly as for a
squash, and are recorded so post-commit never condenses into one. Unlike a
squash, the staged files a redo inherited for are no evidence of new session
work: the reset put them back in the worktree and the next turn end records
them as touched again, though the session did nothing new to them. A staged
path counts as held only when the newest dropped commit that changed it
carries a checkpoint this clone has (a trailer whose capture failed still
links, but holds nothing) and the staged mode matches too. Session matching
ignores held paths, so a commit that only redoes linked work gets no fresh
trailer, and one that also stages other session work gets one for that work.
Session matching reads the same rename-free staged paths the redo compared.

stamps nothing and so condenses nothing, post-commit drops them from
the touched files of this worktree's sessions when the commit holds the
recorded content, as carry-forward would; other touched files, steps and
transcript growth stay pending. When a fresh trailer is stamped, post-commit

### Checkpoint ID Linking

The checkpoint ID is the **stable identifier** that links user commits to metadata across branches.

**Format:** one of two shapes — do **not** assume a fixed width:
- **Legacy 12-hex** random ID (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`) — the git-branch store's format.
- **26-char ULID** (Crockford base32, e.g., `01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN`) — minted only
  under the git-refs checkpoint store. A ULID's leading chars encode a millisecond
  timestamp (so it is lexicographically time-sortable) and its tail is random; front
  prefixes are therefore ambiguous — trim ULIDs from nowhere / show them in full for
  display (see `id.CheckpointID.DisplayShort`), and use `id.MaxIDLength`, not a
  hardcoded 12, when reasoning about maximum width.

Both formats are validated by `id.KindOf` / `id.Validate`; readers accept either.

**Read routing (`checkpoint.Open` → `kindRoutingStore`):** id-keyed reads resolve
across both git backends by the checkpoint's format, so a repo running git-refs
and git-branch side by side (or mid-migration) reads either format without
reconfiguring:
- A **ULID** is read from the git-refs store only — never the branch.
- A **hex** ID is read from the active (configured) primary first; when the
  primary is git-refs it also falls back to the git-branch store (a hex checkpoint
  may still sit on the pre-migration v1 branch, or have been migrated into refs).
- `List` unions both backends. **Creates (`Session`) are not kind-routed** — they
  go to the configured primary (+ mirrors); the minted ID already matches the

**Only the final trailer block links a commit** (`stampedTrailer`,
`stampedTrailersOf`, attach's `resolveCheckpointID`, `explain --generate`).
Every path that writes to a checkpoint because a commit names it reads the
commit's final trailer block by git's grammar: no leading whitespace, indented
lines only as continuations of a trailer, and never the subject paragraph. An
`Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere else in the message (pasted, quoted,
indented, or mentioned in prose) names a checkpoint the commit did not stamp,
so prepare-commit-msg stamps a fresh trailer and post-commit condenses there.
Prepare reads the message as git will record it: an editor message loses its
`#` lines and everything from a scissors line down, while a `-m`/`-F` message
keeps `#` lines as content. Read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution,
read-only explain) and squash and redo inheritance still scan the whole
message, because squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the
body. The trailer writer uses the same grammar, so a trailer it appends is
always one the readers accept.

package strategy

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil"
)

func TestStampedTrailer_SkipsInheritedTrailers(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	inherited := id.CheckpointID("01M2VBJBJQZ2BP1W2PBWDF3J30")
	fresh := id.CheckpointID("01M2VBJBJQZ2BP1W2PBWDF3J31")
	msg := "Squashed\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: " + inherited.String() + "\nEntire-Checkpoint: " + fresh.String() + "\n"

	got, ok := stampedTrailer(context.Background(), msg, []id.CheckpointID{inherited})
	assert.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, fresh, got)

	_, ok = stampedTrailer(context.Background(), "Squashed\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: "+inherited.String()+"\n", []id.CheckpointID{inherited})
	assert.False(t, ok, "an inherited trailer alone is not a stamp")

	got, ok = stampedTrailer(context.Background(), msg, nil)
	assert.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, inherited, got, "with nothing inherited the first trailer is the stamp, as before")
}

func TestPickCondensationTarget(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	a, b, c := id.CheckpointID("01M2VBJBJQZ2BP1W2PBWDF3J3A"), id.CheckpointID("01M2VBJBJQZ2BP1W2PBWDF3J3B"), id.CheckpointID("01M2VBJBJQZ2BP1W2PBWDF3J3C")
	existing := map[id.CheckpointID]bool{a: true, b: true}
	exists := func(cpID id.CheckpointID) bool { return existing[cpID] }

	got, ok := pickCondensationTarget([]id.CheckpointID{a}, nil)
	assert.True(t, ok)

content.thinking:
Testing against over 1500 random messages, my reader never accepts a checkpoint that git would reject, and it's actually stricter in 36 cases involving git's comment-skipping, the 25% rule, and CRLF handling — so the direction is safe. I also want to double-check that edge case with the Signed-off-by continuation line that git accepted.

Looking more closely, git treats the "\r"-only first line as blank, then reads the indented "Entire-Checkpoint" line as a continuation of the Signed-off-by trailer rather than its own separate trailer — my substring-based check mistakenly flagged this as git accepting it, but it's just a measurement artifact that still falls on the safe side. Now I want to cross-check the Review Lessons against the diff in General.md and cli.md: the guard tests were verified RED on the planted pre-fix violation, which checks out.

I'm also confirming that an updated signature only affects the test interface, not semantics, and that main's broad RemoveCheckpointTrailers behavior was intentionally left untouched. The RED test run exercised the correct failure branch — the not-found error, not an earlier unrelated failure — and the integration test's precondition assertions confirm setup worked properly. I also note the PR has already been merged with current main as required.

The fail-closed strict reader only rejects non-final-block mentions, leaving read-only discovery paths unchanged, which satisfies the guard-only-against-the-targeted-failure principle. For the corpus validation concern, I'll be careful to describe my property check as using a synthetic vocabulary rather than overstating it as real corpus validation, and I confirm no git subprocess was replaced since we're parsing git's own grammar directly. Docs have been updated per CLAUDE.md's guidance to keep architecture docs current, though I'm weighing whether CLAUDE.md itself needs a new section on trailer parsing.

Now I'm drafting the fix commit message explaining that an Entire-Checkpoint line anywhere in a commit message was deciding which checkpoint a commit wrote to, since main's provenance check only refuses checkpoints that already exist locally -- this caused attach to write sessions into any mentioned checkpoint, prepare-commit-msg to skip adding trailers because it misread body lines as already stamped, and explain --generate to resolve the wrong mention. The fix requires reading only the final trailer block.

I'm also noting that read-only lookups, squash/redo inheritance, and checkpoint delete should keep scanning the whole message since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrapping up with the commit's Fixes tags and co-author attribution.

Since #2256 is already closed via the cherry-picked commit, this commit's message should just say "Fixes #2255," with the PR body carrying both. While waiting for background tests, I'll compute the diff stat and do a final review pass over the uncommitted changes.
No false acceptances across 1,500 random messages, with 36 cases where it was stricter than git (the safe direction). I'll review my uncommitted diff while the suites finish running.

content.text:
The fix is done and verified, and stops here for your review. Three commits are on the #2253 branch locally (not pushed). The fix itself is uncommitted, as you asked.

**Committed on `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`:**
- `fc529286b` and `d5f03a604`: #2259's two writer commits, cherry-picked cleanly.
- `7c2834865`: a merge of `upstream/main` (`ee70a6747`). Every file outside `cmd/entire/cli/trailers` takes main's version and the migration files stay deleted. After this commit the branch differs from main only in the trailers package (the strict reader plus #2259's writer).

**Uncommitted fix (10 files changed, 1 new):**

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `trailers.go` | The subject paragraph never counts as trailers, matching git. New `StripEditorComments` drops `#` lines and everything from the scissors line down. Stale doc comment fixed. |
| `manual_commit_provenance.go` | `stampedTrailer` and `stampedTrailersOf` read only the final trailer block. New `preparedFinalTrailers` cleans editor messages; `-m`/`-F` messages keep `#` lines as content. |
| `manual_commit_hooks.go` | Both `stampedTrailer` callers pass the source. The amend handler preserves only a final-block trailer and keeps main's deleted-ID handling. |
| `attach.go` | `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID` read the final block. |
| `explain.go` | `--generate` reads the final block; read-only explain keeps whole-message discovery. |
| `manual_commit_provenance_test.go` | Signature update only. |
| `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` | One paragraph on which trailer grants permission to write. |
| Tests | `trailers_test.go` (subject rule, OPF, writer), `attach_test.go` (3), `explain_test.go` (2), and new `integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` (5) |

**Tests first:**
- **Failing before the fix:** 3 subject-rule unit cases, 3 attach tests, the explain `--generate` test, and 4 of the 5 hook-flow integration tests. Each failed for the expected reason; for example, prepare-commit-msg added no trailer.
- **Guards, already passing:** the read-only explain test and the `commit -v --amend` integration test.
- **After the fix:** all of them pass, and so do main's existing squash and redo adversarial tests.

**Full verification:**
- **Format and lint:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint` reports 0 issues; `fmt` changed nothing.
- **Integration:** 808 tests, 0 failures, with a freshly built `entire` first on PATH.
- **Canary:** vogon 53/53 and roger-roger 4/4.
- **Unit:** 15,012 tests, 4 failures, all in code this change doesn't touch:
  - `TestResolveClaudeConfigDir_PrefersClaudesAnswer`
  - `TestDiscoverAndRegister_ContinuesAfterRegistrationError`
  - `TestInstallHooks_ReclaimedChainRunsEachHookOnce`, which counts twice (the test and its subtest)

  Each stopped at a timeout while the machine was busy, and all pass when rerun on their own.
- **Random-message checks** (synthetic messages, throwaway, nothing added to the repo):
  - Writer to reader: 0 misses in 20,000 messages.
  - Writer to `git interpret-trailers`: 0 misses in 500.
  - Our reader never accepted a checkpoint that git rejects (0 of 1,500).

**Review Lessons:** no violations. The "review against current main" lesson is covered by the merge with main.

**Proposed commit message:**
```
fix(checkpoints): require the final trailer block before writing to a checkpoint

An Entire-Checkpoint line anywhere in a commit message still decided which
checkpoint a commit wrote to. Main's provenance check only refuses a
checkpoint that already exists locally, so:

- attach wrote the attached session into any checkpoint the message
  mentioned, even mid-sentence
- prepare-commit-msg treated a body line as already stamped and added no
  trailer, so post-commit either condensed the session's work under an ID
  this clone does not have or, when it did have it, linked nothing
- explain --generate resolved the first mention anywhere in the message

Read the final trailer block instead, by git's grammar, wherever a commit's
trailer decides a write: stampedTrailer and stampedTrailersOf, the amend
handler, attach's planAttachLink and resolveCheckpointID, and explain's
--generate paths. Prepare reads the message as git will record it: an editor
message loses its "#" lines and everything from a scissors line down, while
a -m/-F message keeps "#" lines as content. The final-block reader no longer
treats the subject paragraph as trailers, matching git.

Read-only lookups, squash and redo inheritance, and checkpoint delete keep
scanning the whole message: squash commits carry their squashed commits'
trailers in the body.

Fixes #2255

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Not done yet, each needing your approval:**
- **Push.** It will be an ordinary push, no force, because the branch only gained commits.
- **The new #2253 description,** which I'll show you in full first.
- **The comment closing #2259.**

Two follow-ups are left out: `core.commentChar` support, and the `-m … -e` case where a trailer could be added twice.

In entireio/cli the quality bar is *evidence*, not code volume. Stefan Haubold (`Soph`) wrote 25 of the last 60 commits as of 2026-08-14 and sets the house style. Diffs are often tiny (#1985 was +6/-1); PR bodies are lab notebooks.

The beat order every exemplar PR follows: **Problem** (failure quoted verbatim, real log/CI output) → **Cause** (traced to a specific commit, often by diffing logs from the last green run) → **Fix** (framed as removing an asymmetry, reusing an existing helper, not adding a mechanism) → **Why nothing caught it** (explicit coverage-gap post-mortem) → **Tests, "Verified RED"** (named tests plus the exact pre-fix failure message) → **Rejected alternatives** (with cost, e.g. "~4 signatures and ~45 call sites") → **Test plan checkboxes** ending in `mise run check`.

Two habits worth copying: performance claims use **interleaved** A/B runs with medians (sequential runs let the first arm absorb cold page-cache cost and invert the result — stated in both #1985 and #1968), and negative/deflated results get reported honestly (#1985 talked itself down from a 49% headline to 2%).

**Why:** matching this format is the highest-leverage thing for getting contributions merged fast, and it is doable before deep Go fluency.
**How to apply:** write the failing test first so its real output becomes the "Verified RED" line — the test discipline and the PR-body discipline are the same act. Full playbook artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/0228a8ac-84b6-413e-bd05-5621d7dfb4f3 . See [[entire-1927-contribution-thread]].

After pushing, GitHub will recompute mergeability, though fork PRs still need maintainer CI approval; I also note the old #2259 branch will linger and could be cleaned up separately later. I'm drafting a new PR title, "fix(checkpoints): require the final trailer block before writing to a checkpoint," to better match the commit, and starting on a PR body in their house style.

I'm writing the body to explain that any `Entire-Checkpoint:` line in a commit message, no matter where it appears, still determines which checkpoint gets written to, because main's provenance check only blocks IDs that already exist locally, not ones pasted or quoted elsewhere. I'm folding in that this PR absorbs #2259's trailer-writer fix, since the stricter reader here is what exposed that writer bug, so they need to merge together. I'm building a table of scenarios reproduced on current main, showing cases like `entire attach` or `git commit -m` with a stray `Entire-Checkpoint:` line causing two unrelated sessions to collide in the same checkpoint.

Now I'm explaining the root cause: every place deciding whether a write is allowed uses an unanchored trailer-parsing regex that scans the entire message, which is correct for discovery but wrong for authority since squash commits legitimately carry old trailers in their bodies. The fix is to make only the final trailer block, per git's trailer grammar, authoritative for writes, affecting `stampedTrailer`, `stampedTrailersOf`, and the amend handler.

I'm also deciding what stays unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups like resume, status, attribution, and read-only explain, plus squash/redo inheritance and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which intentionally stays broad so deletes remove every related trailer. Prepare and attach need to agree on the same message-stripping rules git itself applies, and the writer and readers must share the same trailer-block grammar so anything appended is always something the readers will accept.

Looking at why nothing caught this earlier, the existing provenance and adversarial tests only exercised inherited trailers from squash and redo, never a message that merely mentioned an ID in the body, so attach and explain had no coverage for that case. I verified several integration tests were RED on main before the fix — the trailer authority tests for body-line and indented-line mentions of unknown or existing checkpoints, plus the agent-commit-with-body-line case, all failed because prepare-commit-msg wasn't stamping the trailer in the final block, while the verbose-amend guard test correctly passed as a sanity check. The attach-side tests for body, indented, and prose-mentioned checkpoint IDs also failed, confirming attach was incorrectly selecting a checkpoint based on a mere mention rather than an actual trailer.

I also ran a throwaway property check across 20,000 randomly constructed messages with various line types (plain, indented, continuation, comment, CRLF, trailer-shaped subjects), confirming the writer's output always round-tripped correctly through the final-block reader and matched git's own trailer parser, with the reader erring only on the stricter, safer side in the rare mismatches. Then I considered and rejected anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts as a fix, since it still lets body lines steer writes and breaks squash discovery for indented cases.

Checking only for checkpoint existence is also insufficient, since existence alone doesn't confirm this commit stamped it and misses unfetched IDs. I also decided against carrying over the earlier `core.commentChar` detection since its `auto` mode mis-picks the character once git writes its comment block -- main hard-codes `#`, so that's a separate change.

There's a known gap: `-m -e` commits report source `message` but git still strips comments, so a message with an existing trailer above git's comment block could get duplicated -- rare and consistent with how main already treats `#` for that source. For branch history, I merged current main, resolved conflicts in favor of main's provenance model (removing the legacy migration), then reapplied the final-block reads to main's call sites in the last commit, so the diff against main is what matters and a squash-merge is recommended.

content.text:
Main already stops a leftover mention of a *deleted* checkpoint from counting (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`, which still passes with this change), but not a live or unfetched one. That's the honest "why nothing caught it". Main has moved to `f36367e6f`, and the branch still merges into it cleanly.

The fix is committed locally as `9dcb3f66f`. Nothing has been pushed or posted. The branch preflight reports **Ready: yes** (diff check passes, no secret or debug lines, 11 files against `upstream/main`). Here are the three things to approve.

## 1. Push plan

```bash
git -C /Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block push origin fix-checkpoint-trailer-block
```

- **Target:** `origin` = `MuskanPaliwal/cli`, branch `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`, which is PR #2253's head (base `entireio/cli:main`).
- **Ordinary fast-forward, no force:** from `7be8499d4` to `9dcb3f66f`. Most of the 1,748 commits ahead are main's commits from the merge, already on GitHub.
- **No Trail:** `work` creates none for fork PRs.
- **After the push:** GitHub should show #2253 as mergeable again, and a maintainer has to approve the fork CI runs.

**Proposed new #2253 title** (matches the commit; the current one is "trust only final trailer blocks for mutations"):
`fix(checkpoints): require the final trailer block before writing to a checkpoint`

## 2. New #2253 description

```markdown
Fixes #2255
Fixes #2256

An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere in a commit message still decides which checkpoint a commit writes to. Main's provenance check (`stampedByAnotherCommit`) only refuses a checkpoint that already exists in the local store, so a checkpoint ID in a commit body, whether pasted, quoted, indented, or mentioned mid-sentence, still steers three writes.

This PR now also carries #2259 (the trailer writer fix). The stricter reader here is what makes that writer bug reachable, so the two need to land together, and I'm closing #2259 in favour of this one.

## Problem

I ported the scenarios onto current main and ran them there:

| Scenario on main | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `entire attach` on a commit whose body says `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` | The attached session is written into `<id>`, which ends up holding two unrelated sessions. Same for an indented line and for "Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: <id> from last week." |
| `git commit -m` with that line in the body, `<id>` not in this clone | prepare-commit-msg treats it as already stamped and adds no trailer. Post-commit then condenses the session's work under `<id>`, claiming an ID that may belong to a teammate's unfetched checkpoint. |
| Same, `<id>` already in this clone | Post-commit correctly refuses to write there, but the commit ends up with no checkpoint at all. |
| `entire explain --commit <sha> --generate` | Resolves the first mention anywhere in the message. |

## Cause

Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers with `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints`, whose regex is unanchored and scans the whole message. That is right for discovery, since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrong for deciding a write.

## Fix

Only the final trailer block, read by git's grammar, decides a write:

- `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (post-commit)
- the amend handler, which still treats a deleted ID mentioned anywhere as stripped, as main does
- attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, switched together so joining and resolving agree
- explain's `--generate` paths; read-only explain keeps whole-message discovery

Prepare reads the message as git will record it: an editor message loses its `#` lines and everything from a scissors line down (`trailers.StripEditorComments`), while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps `#` lines as content, the same rule `addInheritedCheckpointTrailer` already follows. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, and never reads the subject paragraph as trailers. The writer from #2259 uses the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.

Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution, read-only explain), squash and redo inheritance, and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.

## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

I merged current main into this branch first, so the call sites below were main's code when these failed:

- `integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` drives the real prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hook binaries. `TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint`, `TestTrailerAuthority_IndentedLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint`, `TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingExistingCheckpoint` and `TestTrailerAuthority_AgentCommitWithBodyLine` failed with `prepare-commit-msg must stamp a trailer in the final block`. `TestTrailerAuthority_VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` is a guard: it passes before and after, and fails if the editor-message cleanup is skipped.
- `TestAttach_BodyCheckpointLineDoesNotSelectCheckpoint`, `TestAttach_IndentedCheckpointLineDoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestAttach_CheckpointMentionedInProseDoesNotSelectCheckpoint` failed with `attach wrote the session into checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6, which the commit only mentions in its body`.
- `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer` failed with `references checkpoint deadbeefcafe via its Entire-Checkpoint trailer: checkpoint not found`. `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` guards discovery.
- The subject-paragraph cases in `trailers_test.go` failed before that rule was added.

I also ran a throwaway property check over random messages built from a fixed set of lines (plain, indented, continuation, `#`, CRLF, trailer-shaped subjects). In 20,000 messages the writer's output was always read back by the final-block reader, all 500 sampled outputs parsed in `git interpret-trailers --parse`, and in 1,500 messages the reader never accepted a checkpoint that git rejects. It was stricter than git in 36, which is the safe direction.

## Rejected alternatives

- Anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts: a body line could still steer writes, and indented squash messages would stop being discovered.
- Checking only that the named checkpoint exists: existence says nothing about whether this commit stamped it, and it misses IDs this clone has not fetched.
- Keeping this PR's earlier `core.commentChar` detection: its `auto` mode picks the wrong character once git has written its comment block. Main hard-codes `#` today, so comment-character support belongs in a separate change.

## Known gap

`git commit -m … -e` reports source `message` while git still strips comments, so a `-m` message whose own trailer sits above git's comment block could get a second trailer. It is rare, and matches how main already treats `#` lines for that source.

## Branch history

This branch predates main's provenance model. I merged current main, resolved every call-site conflict to main's version (the legacy migration this PR used to touch is gone), and re-applied the final-block reads to main's call sites in the last commit. The diff against main is the change to review.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run fmt && mise run lint`: 0 issues
- [x] `mise run test`: 15,012 tests; 4 failures in unrelated packages (claude config probe, external agent discovery, hook chain) that timed out under load and pass in isolation
- [x] `mise run test:integration`: 808 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `mise run test:e2e:canary`: vogon 53/53, roger-roger 4/4
- [ ] CI, once a maintainer approves the fork workflow run

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

